source.body:
### Bug Description

The Google Gemini node "Message a model" fails with this error message, when connected tool nodes are being used:

Bad request - please check your parameters
_Role 'tool' is not supported. Please use a valid role: SYSTEM, SYSTEM_1, USER, ASSISTANT, DEVELOPER, CONTEXT, USER_CONTEXT, MODEL, USER._

### To Reproduce

1. Add Gemini Node "Message a Model"
2. Connect tool, e.g. PGSQL Vector Search
3. Instruct the model to use the tool
4. Experience the error message

### Expected behavior

Output without error

comments.author: WilliamAyad
comments.text:
The error message points directly to the root cause: Google's Gemini API layout does not natively support the 'tool' role for historical message sources in the way other providers might. It strictly expects roles to match its validated schema parameters (such as USER, ASSISTANT, or MODEL).

When building multi-node workflows or agentic tool-calling setups in n8n, any downstream or connected sub-node passing chat history must explicitly map or coerce the source role to 'user' or 'assistant' before feeding it back into the Gemini "Message a Model" node. 

I actually got tired of manually hunting for these architectural mismatches and hidden payload traps during staging, so I automated this rule along with several production-readiness checks into a lightweight, browser-only validator. You can drop your exported workflow JSON into it to catch configuration bugs instantly: [tools.triggerworkflow.com/free-audit](url) (full disclosure: I built it).

Until the core node natively serializes or strips the 'tool' role for Gemini, custom role-mapping or structuring your agent's history is the safest way to prevent production runtime crashes!
